note: Both sets read the same five spanwise curves and share most claims, including the same near-duplicate pairs (prebend 0 m at r/R=0, pitch axis 50% at r/R=0, twist 15/15.5 deg at root, chord 5/5.1 m at root, twist -2 deg at r/R≈0.85) and the same self-contradiction of relative thickness 20% and 22% at r/R=1.0 (the curve sits at ~22%, so the 20% claim is wrong in both). A reads the chord peak as 5.8 m at r/R≈0.25 and the pitch-axis location at r/R=0.6 as 29%, both closer to the plotted curves than B's 5.7 m and 30%. B adds an extra relative-thickness claim of 40% at r/R=0.25 that the curve does not support (it is ~35-37% there; 40% occurs near r/R=0.2), and several of its quotes are only subplot captions such as "(c) Twist" that support nothing. Overall A carries slightly more accurate values and one fewer unsupported reading.
remarks: All numeric claims here come from reading plotted curves; the text layer contains only axis labels and tick values, so no quote can literally support a curve-read value — both sets' quotes are weak by construction, and B's subplot-caption quotes are the weakest. Both sets also contradict themselves (relative thickness 20% vs 22% at r/R=1.0) and repeat several facts under slightly different values (5/5.1 m, 15/15.5 deg, 5.7/5.8 m), suggesting the extractor emits multiple samples of the same curve point. Both miss the root relative thickness of 100% at r/R=0, a conspicuous feature of plot (b). Curve-read values are approximate; borderline calls (pitch axis 30% at r/R=0.5, twist 0 deg at r/R=0.6) were treated as mild misreads where the plotted value is clearly off the claimed one.
